questions.stem: A note gives configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3

options.text: The element is silicon with 14 electrons
The element is phosphorus with 15 electrons
The element is sulfur with 16 electrons
The element is aluminum with 13 electrons

questions.explanation: Summing gives 15 electrons, atomic number 15, phosphorus. Silicon, sulfur, and aluminum have different counts.
questions.hint: Sum the electrons to get the atomic number.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Determine charge of an ion with more electrons
questions.stem: A note gives an atom with 17 protons and 18 electrons; ion charge
questions.explanation: Charge = 17 - 18 = -1. The ion is Cl- with a -1 charge.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Find neutrons for a common isotope
questions.stem: A note gives oxygen-16 with atomic number 8; neutron count

options.text: Neutrons equal 16 from the mass number
Neutrons equal 8 from the atomic number
Neutrons equal 8 from 16 minus 8
Neutrons equal 24 from 16 plus 8

questions.explanation: Neutrons = 16 - 8 = 8. Using either number alone or adding gives wrong counts.
questions.hint: Subtract atomic number from mass number.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Solve abundance for a two-isotope element
questions.stem: A note gives average mass 6.94 amu for lithium isotopes 6 and 7; explain abundance of 6

answer.exemplar: Set 6x + 7(1-x) = 6.94, solve x = 0.06, so lithium-6 has 6% abundance and lithium-7 has 94%.

questions.explanation: Solving gives x = 0.06, so 6% abundance for Li-6. Simple average would give 50% which is wrong.
questions.hint: Set up a weighted average equation.
